label: Loneliness & homesickness
title: Bhagavad Gita for Loneliness & Homesickness: 7 Verses
description: Seven verses for being far from home or alone among people, from 'I am never lost to you' (6.30) to being the friend you need (12.13). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try.
h1: Bhagavad Gita for loneliness and homesickness: 7 verses
subtitle: For a new city, an empty flat, or a full house that still feels lonely. Read one a day, or all seven tonight.
intro: Krishna calls himself the friend of every being (5.29) and places the divine in every heart (18.61). These verses are for anyone alone in a new city, far from family, or lonely in a full house. They move from the promise that you're never lost to the one who sees you (6.30), to the list of everything Krishna says he is to us, home and friend included (9.18), and then turn outward: feeling others' joy and pain as your own, and being the friend you need. The last is from the Ramayana, two exiles who swore friendship over a fire.

days.heading: You are never lost to him
days.line: See me in everything and everything in me, and I never lose you, nor you me.
days.forYou: Krishna says that whoever sees him everywhere, and everything in him, is never lost to him, and he is never lost to them (na praṇaśyati). Loneliness feels like being lost to everyone. This verse names one bond that distance can't break.
days.today: Step outside for five minutes tonight and look at the sky. The same sky is over home.

days.heading: Someone lives in your heart
days.line: The divine lives in the heart of every being, yours included.
days.forYou: Īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati. Krishna places the divine in the heart of every being, which means in yours, here, in this flat and this city, as much as back home or in a temple.
days.today: Sit quietly for two minutes with a hand on your chest. Just notice that you're there.

days.heading: Home, shelter, friend
days.line: I am your goal, your support, your witness, your home, your shelter and your friend.
days.forYou: In one verse Krishna lists what he is to every being: goal, support, witness, home (nivāsaḥ), shelter (śaraṇam) and friend (suhṛt). If you've been missing all of those, this verse names them together.
days.today: Make your space feel like home in one small way: a lamp, a photo, or a smell from home cooking.

days.heading: The friend of all beings
days.line: The divine is the well-wisher of every being, you included. Knowing this, you find peace.
days.forYou: Suhṛdaṃ sarva-bhūtānām: Krishna is the well-wisher of every being, and knowing this, he says, brings peace. That peace can come on a quiet evening with no calls, because someone wishes you well all the same.
days.today: Call or message someone from home today. Tell them one ordinary thing about your day.

days.heading: Feel their joy and pain as yours
days.line: Feel others' joy and pain as if they were your own. That is the highest practice.
days.forYou: The highest practice, Krishna says, is to feel others' joy and sorrow as if they were your own. Loneliness turns attention inward. This verse turns it outward, and that's often where connection starts.
days.today: Ask one colleague or neighbour a real question about their week, and listen to the answer.

days.heading: Be the friend
days.line: Hate no one. Be friendly and kind, free of 'mine' and ego, steady in pain and joy, and forgiving.
days.forYou: Krishna describes the person dear to him as friendly and compassionate (maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca), hating no one. You can't make people reach out to you, and you can be the friendly one first. It counts even when nothing comes back right away.
days.today: Invite one person for tea, a walk or a call this week.

days.heading: Two exiles and a fire

story.title: Ram and Sugriva become friends
story.body: Ram had lost his home, and his wife Sita had been taken. Sugriva, driven out by his brother, had lost his home and his wife too. They met in the forest and swore friendship before a fire. Then Sugriva brought out the jewels Sita had dropped as she was carried away. Ram broke down at the sight of them, and Sugriva, who had his own grief, comforted him: in trouble, think it through steadily, and lean on your friend.
story.lesson: Two people in trouble can carry each other.

days.forYou: Far from home, the friends who matter are often the people who understand what you've lost.
days.today: Find one person who's also far from home and suggest meeting up.

verse.sanskrit: आढ्यो वापि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा । निर्दोषश्च सदोषश्च वयस्यः परमा गतिः ॥
verse.line: Rich or poor, happy or sad, flawed or not, a friend is your greatest refuge.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about loneliness?
faq.a: Krishna says he is never lost to the one who sees him everywhere (6.30), that the divine lives in the heart of every being (18.61), and that he is the friend of all beings (5.29). In 9.18 he calls himself our home, shelter and friend.

faq.q: Is there a Gita verse for being far from home?
faq.a: 9.18 names Krishna as home (nivāsaḥ), shelter and friend, and 18.61 places the divine in every heart wherever you are. Many people living abroad keep one of these by them.

faq.q: What does the Gita say about friendship?
faq.a: Krishna describes the person dear to him as friendly and compassionate to all (12.13), and calls himself the well-wisher of every being (5.29). The highest practice, he says, is to feel others' joy and pain as your own (6.32).
